info.title: Hodei-Shield API
info.summary: Third-party risk and compliance posture, for your own systems.
info.description:
## Versioning

`/v1` is frozen. These changes are **compatible** and will happen inside it
without notice:

- a new operation;
- a new **optional** query parameter;
- a new field in a response object;
- a new value in a field documented as an open vocabulary (`status`,
  `severity`, `evidence_type`, the keys of `by_status`);
- a new `error.code`, always with the HTTP status its siblings already use;
- anything under `error.details`, which is diagnostic and not part of the
  contract.

Write your client so those do not break it: ignore unknown fields, do not
switch exhaustively on a documented-open vocabulary, and treat an unknown
`error.code` as "an error of this HTTP status".

These changes are **incompatible** and will NOT happen inside `/v1`. They go
to `/v2`, and `/v1` keeps serving:

- removing or renaming an operation, a parameter or a field;
- changing the type, the unit or the meaning of a field;
- making an optional parameter required, or narrowing what one accepts;
- changing which scope an operation requires;
- changing the HTTP status an existing `error.code` is sent with.

## Read-only

`/v1` only reads. Every operation is a `GET`. Any other method (`POST`, `PUT`,
`PATCH`, `DELETE`) on a path that exists answers **405** with `Allow: GET`, and on
a path that does not exist answers **404**: neither changes any state. A write
will be offered only as a new operation, which is a compatible change, once a
customer asks for a concrete one.

## Authentication

Every operation takes `Authorization: Bearer <tenant API key>`. A key belongs
to ONE tenant and carries an explicit list of scopes; it can read nothing
outside that tenant, whatever it asks for. Each operation below declares the
scope it requires. A key that authenticates but lacks the scope is answered
**403**, never 404: you are told what you are missing, not that the resource
does not exist.

## Errors

Every error has the same body:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "forbidden", "message": "…", "request_id": "…" } }
```

Branch on `code`, log `request_id`, show `message` to nobody but yourself.
`request_id` is also the `X-Request-Id` response header, and it is what
support will ask you for.

## Rate limits

Every response that got past authentication carries the limit that is closest
to being exhausted:

- `RateLimit-Limit` — requests allowed in the window;
- `RateLimit-Remaining` — requests left in the current window;
- `RateLimit-Reset` — **seconds** until the window renews;
- `RateLimit-Policy` — `<limit>;w=<window seconds>`.

Three limits apply, each per one-minute window: per API key, per organisation
(all of its keys together) and per service. The first two come from the licence
of the organisation the key belongs to: a higher licence tier has more room, and
an MSSP partner has more than a direct customer of the same tier. Read the
current limit from `RateLimit-Limit` and `RateLimit-Policy` rather than
hard-coding it. When one is exhausted the answer is
**429** with `error.code: "rate_limited"`, `Retry-After` (seconds) and
`error.details.scope` (`key`, `tenant` or `service`) saying which. Your
organisation's usage never counts against another's. Windows are fixed, so a
client can burst up to twice the limit across a window boundary: back off on
`Retry-After` rather than pacing to the second. The limits are part of the
service, not of the frozen contract: they may be raised without notice.

## Pagination, filtering and ordering

Every collection takes `page` and `per_page` (max 200) and answers with a
`pagination` object carrying `total` and `total_pages`. Every collection
takes `sort` (an enum of the fields THAT collection can order by) and
`order` (`asc`/`desc`, default `desc`). Filters are exact matches unless
the parameter says otherwise.

The tenant third-party inventory, newest first by default. Soft-deleted vendors are never returned.

Required scope: `supply_risk:read`. Published in `/v1` since 2026-09-20.

parameters.description: Field to order by. One of: created_at, updated_at, name.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring of the name or the domain.

RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests allowed in the window that is closest to being exhausted.

id.description: Stable identifier of the vendor in this tenant.

legal_name.description: Registered legal name, when it differs.

category.description: Free-text category assigned by the tenant.

access_level.description: Level of access the vendor has to the tenant systems.

business_criticality.description: low | medium | high | critical, as set by the tenant.

economic_impact.description: Estimated economic impact of an outage, in the tenant currency.

active.description: Whether the vendor is operationally enabled.

last_scan_at.description: RFC 3339, UTC. Null if never scanned.

lei.description: Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442), for DORA RoI.

items.description: A third party in the tenant inventory.

code.description: Closed vocabulary; new members may be added (see Versioning).

message.description: For a human reading a log. Not stable; do not parse it.

details.description: Diagnostic. Not part of the frozen contract.

bearerAuth.description: A tenant API key, created in the console under Settings → API keys with the minimum scopes it needs.

oauth2.description: A USER access token (`hs_at_…`) issued by the HodeiShield console, the OAuth 2.1 authorization server at `https://app.hodeishield.com/api/auth` (metadata: `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` on its origin). Authorization code with PKCE (S256, mandatory) for applications with a browser; the RFC 8628 device authorization grant (`https://app.hodeishield.com/api/auth/device/code`) for those without one. Every token is bound to ONE user and ONE tenant, chosen by the user on the consent screen, and carries read scopes only; the tenant is re-checked against what the user can see on every request. Public clients register themselves (RFC 7591) at `/oauth2/register`; the HodeiShield CLI is pre-registered as `hodeishield-cli`. Revocation: RFC 7009 at `/oauth2/revoke`, or by the user in the console under Account → Application access.
